hints.title: Group Concatenation
hints.text: Group by state and aggregate sorted city names separated by commas using group concatenation.

hints.title: Matching Initial Letter Count
hints.text: Count cities whose first letter matches the first letter of their state using a conditional count: count(case when left(city, 1) = left(state, 1) then 1 end).

hints.title: Group Filter and Sorting
hints.text: Filter states in the having clause having at least 3 cities and matching_letter_count > 0. Sort by matching_letter_count descending, then state ascending.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    state, 
    GROUP_CONCAT(city ORDER BY city ASC SEPARATOR ', ') AS cities,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN LEFT(city, 1) = LEFT(state, 1) THEN 1 END) AS matching_letter_count
FROM cities
GROUP BY state
HAVING 
    COUNT(city) >= 3 
    AND COUNT(CASE WHEN LEFT(city, 1) = LEFT(state, 1) THEN 1 END) > 0
ORDER BY 
    matching_letter_count DESC, 
    state ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Grouping by state and aggregating sorted city names.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per state for string concatenation cause performance degradation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for string aggregation buffers.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies group aggregation with conditional counting and having clause filters.

solutions.code:
SELECT 
    state, 
    GROUP_CONCAT(city ORDER BY city ASC SEPARATOR ', ') AS cities,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN LEFT(city, 1) = LEFT(state, 1) THEN 1 END) AS matching_letter_count
FROM cities
GROUP BY state
HAVING 
    COUNT(city) >= 3 
    AND COUNT(CASE WHEN LEFT(city, 1) = LEFT(state, 1) THEN 1 END) > 0
ORDER BY 
    matching_letter_count DESC, 
    state ASC;

SELECT 
    state, 
    STRING_AGG(city, ', ' ORDER BY city ASC) AS cities,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN LEFT(city, 1) = LEFT(state, 1) THEN 1 END) AS matching_letter_count
FROM cities
GROUP BY state
HAVING 
    COUNT(city) >= 3 
    AND COUNT(CASE WHEN LEFT(city, 1) = LEFT(state, 1) THEN 1 END) > 0
ORDER BY 
    matching_letter_count DESC, 
    state ASC;
